cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says *I will give you rest* to the weary, and Jeremiah shows where Yahuah (the LORD) has always said rest is found, on the old paths, the good way, walked. The invitation sends the tired back onto the road the Father laid out, and the sorrow at the end of Jeremiah's verse, *We will not walk therein*, is the refusal the weary are being called out of.
cards.member_phrase: ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sets the rest at the end of a walk on the old paths, the good way, and records that the people refused it.

cards.prose: The rest offered to those who *labour and are heavy laden* was already being held out in Isaiah to a weary people, and Isaiah's verse closes the way Jeremiah's does, with *they would not hear*. The same refusal runs through both, and it is into that refusal that a man now stands and says come.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah names the rest that eases the weary and says plainly that the people would not hear it.

cards.prose: The ones who *labour and are heavy laden* are not bent under the Father's commandments. The load Yahusha (Jesus) names elsewhere is the one the scribes and Pharisees *bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne*, laid on shoulders by a system that will not lift a finger to move it. The people under it are the ones he calls to himself.
cards.member_phrase: they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names the heavy, grievous load that was bound on the people's shoulders, the weight the weary are called out from.

cards.prose: Peter speaks of a yoke too, one laid on the neck of the disciples *which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear*. The fathers walked the Father's commandments, so this cannot be them. It is the demand pressed on people whose hearts the Father had already cleansed, that they be made something before they were counted in, and it is that weight the call to rest answers.
cards.member_phrase: to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear
cards.member_sentence: Peter names a yoke on the disciples' necks that neither the fathers nor he could bear, the kind of load Yahusha's (Jesus's) call to the weary lifts off.
cards.flag: Old note only said 'Peter's restatement'. The common reading takes this yoke to be the Torah itself; I wrote it as the conversion demand pressed on the disciples (the verses around it speak of hearts cleansed and no difference put), not the commandments. Acts 15:1 is not in the packet context, so please confirm.

cards.prose: Paul tells what he carried before he was called, a zeal for *the traditions of my fathers* that put him ahead of many his own age. That is the human weight laid over the commandments, and it is the sort of burden the weary are told to bring to Yahusha (Jesus). It was never the instruction Moses gave that wore them out.
cards.member_phrase: being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers
cards.member_sentence: Paul names the handed-down traditions he was once zealous for, the human weight laid over the commandments that the weary are called out from.
cards.flag: Medium-confidence pairing. Gal 1:14 does not itself say 'Pharisee'; I tied it to the traditions laid over the commandments as the old note did.

cards.prose: The rest he promises here is not rest apart from the commandment. This is the covenant word to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), that Yahuah (the LORD) would put his law in their inward parts and *write it in their hearts*. What weighs on the weary is what men added, and what he gives is the commandment set back where it was always meant to live.
cards.member_phrase: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts
cards.member_sentence: The covenant promise to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) is the law written in the heart, not set aside, and the rest he offers goes with it.

cards.prose: A man can put down a load, but he cannot take a stony heart out of his own chest. Here the Father says he will do it himself and give *an heart of flesh*. This is what makes the commandment light to carry, and the rest on offer rides on that promise.
cards.member_phrase: I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to take out the stony heart and give a heart of flesh, which is what makes his way light to carry.

cards.prose: John sets the weary beside the commandments themselves. Keeping them is the love of Elohim (God), and they are *not grievous*. So the weight on the weary was never the commandments, and the one who says come and rest is calling them toward the keeping, not away from it.
cards.member_sentence: John says plainly that keeping the commandments is the love of Elohim (God) and that they are not grievous.

cards.prose: Nobody should hear *I will give you rest* as a man putting the law down. The same Yahusha (Jesus) says he is *not come to destroy, but to fulfil*, and the two together show the rest is found with the commandments standing, not with them taken away.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says he did not come to destroy the law or the prophets, so the rest he gives is not a release from the Torah.

cards.prose: *All things are delivered unto me of my Father* is said here before the cross, and after the tomb he says it again as all power given. In both the one who gives is the Father and the one who receives is the Son. The authority was never something the Son took.
cards.member_sentence: After the resurrection the Son says again that all power has been given to him, the same handing over by the Father.

cards.prose: Matthew has the Son saying *neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son*, and John says it from the other side. The Father is unseen, and the Son, who is in his bosom, is the one who has made him known. The one who can be seen is the one who shows the one who cannot.
cards.member_sentence: No man has seen the Father, and the only begotten Son, who is in his bosom, is the one who has declared him.

cards.prose: The Father handing all things to the Son is not the Son acting on his own. John has it from the Son's own mouth, that he does only *what he seeth the Father do*. What the Father gives is what the Son carries out, and that is how he can make the Father known to whomever he will.
cards.member_phrase: The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do
cards.member_sentence: The Son does nothing of himself but what he sees the Father do, so what he reveals is the Father's own.

cards.prose: Matthew says no one knows the Father except the Son and the one the Son chooses to show him. John puts the same thing as a road, *no man cometh unto the Father, but by me*. The Father is the one to be reached, and the Son is the one who opens the way and leads there.
cards.member_sentence: The Son says no man comes to the Father except through him, the same sole access to the Father.
cards.flag: The old note quotes 'He that hath seen me hath seen the Father', which is not the target verse; I wrote to John 14:6 as given.

cards.prose: The Son knows the Father and the Father knows the Son, and here he says *I and my Father are one*. They are one in what they know and what they do, and still Father and Son: the one who receives all things from the Father and the one he calls Father. He is not the Father wearing another face.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says he and the Father are one, the oneness of the Son who receives all things from the Father.

cards.prose: In Matthew we hear the Son thanking the Father and saying all things were delivered to him. Here we stand beside him in prayer, asking the Father to glorify the Son so that the Son may glorify him. There are two speaking, and the Son always turns toward the Father.
cards.member_phrase: Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee
cards.member_sentence: In prayer the Son speaks to the Father as Father, asking to be glorified so that he may glorify the Father in return.

cards.prose: Paul holds the two apart and together. The Father is the one source, and the Son is the one *by whom are all things*. That is Matthew's order, the Father as the source who delivers, and the Son as the one through whom it is known and done.
cards.member_phrase: one Elohim (God), the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him
cards.member_sentence: Paul names one Elohim (God), the Father, from whom are all things, and the Son through whom are all things.

cards.prose: Matthew's Son makes the Father known, and Hebrews says how it came about: the Father *spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets*, and then *Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son* (Hebrews 1:2). The speaker is the Father throughout, and the Son is the one he has spoken by.
cards.member_sentence: The Father spoke to the fathers by the prophets and in these last days by his Son, who is the way he makes himself known.

cards.prose: The Father is unseen and without form, and Paul says the Son is *the image of the invisible Elohim (God)*. That is why Matthew can say no one knows the Father save the Son: the one who is seen is his image, and so the one nobody could look on is made known.
cards.member_sentence: The Son is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the one who can be seen where the Father cannot.

cards.prose: What Yahusha (Jesus) tells John's men to report is out of Isaiah, and at Nazareth he is handed that same book and finds the place. He reads *recovering of sight to the blind* (Luke 4:18), stops at *the acceptable year of Yahuah (Lord)* (Luke 4:19), and closes the scroll, leaving off the day of vengeance that Isaiah's next words name. The works John hears about are the first half of that reading.
cards.member_phrase: there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias
cards.member_sentence: At Nazareth he is handed the same Isaiah scroll whose works he now sends back to John, and he reads it only as far as the acceptable year.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says of John *this is Elias, which was for to come*, and on the way down the mountain the disciples bring up the scribes' question, *Elias must first come*. He answers *Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things* (Matthew 17:11), and then *the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist* (Matthew 17:13).
cards.member_sentence: The disciples ask why the scribes say Elias must first come, and the answer that follows names John as that Elias.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) names Tyre and Sidon as cities that would have repented in sackcloth and ashes at the works done in Chorazin. Tyre had already been spoken to by Yahuah (the LORD) through Ezekiel, against a prince whose *heart is lifted up* (Ezekiel 28:2). It is a city under a word of judgment, and still it is counted better off than the towns that saw him.
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel's word against the prince of Tyre opens here, so Tyre stands under judgment before Yahusha (Jesus) says it will fare better than Chorazin.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the opening line of Ezekiel 28; the card works through the verse after it.

cards.prose: Isaiah's burden of Tyre says what became of the city, *laid waste*, with *no house, no entering in*. Tyre was no stranger to warning, and Yahusha (Jesus) says even Tyre and Sidon *would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes* at the works done in Chorazin and Bethsaida.
cards.member_phrase: it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's burden of Tyre pictures the city laid waste, the judgment already on Tyre that Yahusha (Jesus) says would have turned to repentance had it seen his works.

cards.prose: The city that was burned out of the earth is the one Yahusha (Jesus) says would have *remained until this day* had it seen what Capernaum saw. *Brimstone and fire* fell on Sodom and Gomorrah, and the town that watched the works and shrugged has more to answer for.
cards.member_sentence: Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed by brimstone and fire, the judgment Yahusha (Jesus) says Capernaum has more to answer for than.

cards.prose: He is thanking the Father for what the Father has done, hiding from the wise and prudent and *hast revealed them unto babes*, and he does not claim it as his own doing. John gives the reason: the Son does nothing of himself but what he sees the Father do.
cards.member_phrase: The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do
cards.member_sentence: The Son does nothing of himself but what he sees the Father do, so the revealing he thanks the Father for is the Father's work.

cards.prose: The Father hides from the wise and *hast revealed them unto babes*, and the Son says he knows his sheep and is known of them. The babes are the sheep, and the knowing runs from the Father through the Son to those who are his, not up from anyone's cleverness. The next verse ties it to the Father: *As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father* (John 10:15).
cards.member_sentence: The Son knows his sheep and is known of them, the same knowing the Father and Son share, given to those who are his.

cards.prose: Paul sees the same dividing line. Where the wise and prudent find the word of the cross *foolishness*, to those who are being saved it is the power of Elohim (God). What looks like folly to one hearer is the Father's power to another, and the Father is the one who gives it.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the word of the cross is foolishness to those who perish and the power of Elohim (God) to those being saved.

cards.prose: The Father who has hidden these things and *hast revealed them unto babes* is the one Moses was told no man can look on and live. So what is revealed cannot be got by looking or by cleverness, it has to be given. That is why it matters that the Son, who can be seen, is the one who shows him.
cards.member_sentence: Moses is told no man sees the Father's face and lives, so the Father must be made known by the Son who is seen.
cards.flag: The old note's point (the Son mediating the unseen Father) belongs to Matthew 11:27 more than 11:25; I wrote it against the verse as paired.
